Oelo Permanent Lighting Color Themes Guide: Seasonal Decorating All Year Long

How to use app-controlled color themes to transform your home for every season and holiday — all from your phone.

Published July 21, 2026 · 11 min read · By CleanGutters Lighting, Cherry Hill, NJ

If you're considering permanent Oelo LED roofline lighting — or you've already had it installed — you probably know the biggest selling point: you never have to climb a ladder to hang holiday lights again. What you might not realize is just how much creative control you actually have over the lights once they're up.

Oelo's app-controlled system lets you change the color, brightness, and animation of every light on your roofline from your phone. That means your home can look different every week if you want — warm white for a dinner party, red-white-and-blue for the 4th, purple and orange for Halloween, red and green for Christmas, and soft pastels for Easter.

This guide walks through every seasonal color theme, the exact color settings to use, and tips to make the most of your Oelo lighting system all year round. Whether you're a new permanent lighting owner or just exploring the idea for your South Jersey home, you'll leave knowing exactly how to turn your roofline into a year-round canvas.

Quick stat: Oelo permanent LED lights can reproduce over 16 million colors and support custom scenes that change throughout the evening. Once installed, the only tool you need is the app on your phone — no ladder, no extension cords, no storage bins full of tangled old lights.

How the Oelo Color System Works

Before we dive into seasonal themes, it helps to understand the basics of how Oelo's app controls your lights. The system uses RGB+W (red, green, blue, plus warm white) LEDs that can produce virtually any color. Here are the key controls available in the Oelo app:

Color Zones

Your roofline is divided into zones — typically each face of your house or each architectural element (roofline gables, dormers, garage). The app lets you set different colors for different zones. This means you can do a two-tone scheme like white on the main roofline with red accents on the gable, or set each zone to alternate colors in a pattern.

Brightness Levels

Oelo LEDs are dimmable from 1% to 100%. For daily use, most homeowners keep brightness between 30–50% — enough to create a warm glow that highlights the architecture without being glaring. For holidays and parties, you can bump it up to 70–100% for a bolder statement.

Animation Modes

Beyond static colors, Oelo supports animated effects: fade between colors, twinkle, chase (lights moving along the roofline), pulse, and wave. These are great for holidays — a slow red-white-blue wave for Independence Day, or a twinkle effect for Christmas.

Scheduling

Perhaps the most useful feature: you can schedule color themes to activate automatically. Set your daily "warm white" look to turn on at sunset and off at 11 PM. Then schedule specific themes for holidays to take over automatically on those dates. The app handles it — you don't have to remember to change anything.

Summer Themes (June – August)

South Jersey summers are about backyard barbecues, pool parties, and warm evenings on the patio. Your lighting should support the relaxed, festive summer vibe while staying bright enough to illuminate your outdoor space.

Summer

Warm Amber Glow

Best for: Daily use, dinner parties, quiet evenings

Amber · Warm Orange · Soft Peach

A warm amber glow is the most popular year-round setting. It mimics the color temperature of traditional incandescent lighting and gives your home a welcoming, high-end appearance. Set brightness to 40% for daily use. This single color makes your home look like it's professionally lit every night — which, of course, it is.

Summer

Patriotic (4th of July)

Best for: Independence Day, Memorial Day, Labor Day

Red · White · Blue

Set your roofline zones to alternate between red, white, and blue. For best results: set the main roofline to red on the left third, white in the middle third, and blue on the right third. Add a slow wave animation for a subtle live-flag effect. We covered 4th of July lighting setups in detail here — but as a refresher: use brightness 60–80%, schedule it from sunset to midnight, and your home becomes the block party destination without a single strand of temporary lights.

Summer

Pool & Party Mode

Best for: Pool parties, backyard entertaining, cookouts

Cyan · Lavender · Sky Blue

Cool blues and purples create a resort-like atmosphere around a pool or patio. Set the roofline to a slow color fade between cyan and lavender. Keep brightness moderate (40–50%) so the lights complement rather than overpower your outdoor space. For cookouts, switch to a warm amber — cooler colors are great for swimming but warm tones are more appetizing and flattering for outdoor dining.

Fall Themes (September – November)

Fall in South Jersey is a special season. The leaves change, the air turns crisp, and homes take on a cozy, harvest-season feeling. Your lighting should reflect that warmth. This is also when many homeowners transition from summer entertaining to preparing for the holiday season.

Fall

Harvest Gold

Best for: September–October daily use, tailgate parties

Pumpkin Orange · Golden Yellow · Warm Brown

A gradient from deep pumpkin orange at the edges to golden yellow at the center of your roofline. This mimics the colors of changing leaves and gives your home a cozy, seasonal feel. Schedule it to start September 1st and run through October. Set brightness slightly warmer and lower than summer — around 35% — to match the earlier sunsets and cozier evenings.

Fall

Halloween Spooktacular

Best for: October 1–31, Halloween parties

Purple · Neon Orange · Lime Green

Halloween is where Oelo lighting truly shines (pun intended). Set your roofline to Halloween colors — purple as the main color with orange and green as accents on different architectural zones. Add a slow strobe or twinkle animation for a spooky effect. For the actual Halloween night, try a chase animation in alternating purple and orange that slowly moves around the roofline. Brightness at 70–80% for maximum impact. Parents driving through the neighborhood will stop and take photos.

Fall

Thanksgiving Warmth

Best for: November, Thanksgiving, family gatherings

Burnt Orange · Golden Yellow · Warm White

After Halloween, transition to warm harvest colors for Thanksgiving. A static setting of warm white with golden yellow accents on gables and architectural features creates an elegant, welcoming look for family arrivals. Keep it subtle — the warm colors complement the season without competing with indoor holiday decorations. Brightness at 35–45%.

Holiday & Winter Themes (December – February)

This is the season where permanent lighting pays off most dramatically. While your neighbors are untangling extension cords on cold December mornings, you open the Oelo app, tap "Christmas," and your entire house lights up in 3 seconds flat.

Holiday

Classic Christmas

Best for: December 1 – January 1

Christmas Red · Pine Green · Cool White

Alternating red and green along the main roofline is the classic Christmas look. Add cool white on gables and dormers for contrast. The twinkle animation adds festive magic without being distracting. For a more elegant look, use just red and white (no green) — this creates a candy-cane effect that pairs beautifully with white snow if we get any. Schedule it to start December 1st and run through New Year's Day. Brightness at 60% for the holidays.

Holiday

Hanukkah Celebration

Best for: Hanukkah (dates vary)

Blue · White · Gold

A beautiful blue-and-white color scheme with gold accents is perfect for Hanukkah. Set the main roofline to deep blue with white on architectural highlights, and add small gold accent sections to represent the menorah. The effect is elegant, understated, and unmistakably festive.

Holiday

New Year's Eve Elegance

Best for: December 31 – January 1

Gold · Cool White · Midnight Blue

Ring in the new year with gold and white — a sophisticated, celebratory look that stands out from the typical Christmas colors. Midnight blue accents on architectural details create depth. Use the "sparkle" animation effect if available (or slow twinkle). Brightness at 70% for the evening.

Winter

Winter Whites (January – February)

Best for: Post-holiday daily use, snow events

Warm White · Ice Blue · Pale Blue

After the holidays, switch to a cool winter white or ice blue palette. This creates a beautiful effect when snow falls — the warm-toned lights reflect off the snow with a golden glow, while cool white lights create a crisp, modern look. Soft ice blue gives your home an elegant, winter-resort feel that carries through February. Brightness at 30–40%.

Spring Themes (March – May)

Spring in South Jersey brings blooming gardens, longer evenings, and outdoor entertaining season ramping back up. Soft pastels and fresh colors match the season's renewal.

Spring

Easter Pastels

Best for: Easter, spring gatherings

Pink · Lavender · Soft Yellow

Pastel pink, lavender, and soft yellow create a cheerful spring look. Because these are lighter colors, set brightness slightly higher (50–60%) to maintain visibility at dusk. The soft pastels complement blooming spring gardens and create a welcoming feel for Easter egg hunts and family gatherings. Use a slow fade animation to cycle gently between the three colors.

Spring

Fresh Green & Bloom

Best for: April–May daily use

Fresh Green · Sky Blue · Coral

As the trees and gardens come alive, match your lighting to the season. Fresh green tones along the main roofline with sky blue on accent areas, plus a touch of coral on architectural highlights. This is an upbeat, modern look that pairs beautifully with the natural colors of a spring landscape.

Custom Themes for Special Events

Beyond the calendar seasons, Oelo gives you the flexibility to customize for any occasion. Here are some popular custom themes South Jersey homeowners love:

Custom

Sports Team Colors (Eagles, Phillies, Sixers, Flyers)

Show your Philly pride during game season. Set your roofline to midnight green and silver for Eagles Sundays, red and white for Phillies game days, or blue and red for Sixers playoffs. Zone the colors: main roofline in the primary team color, gables and accents in the secondary color. This is a guaranteed conversation starter during watch parties.

Custom

Birthday Party

Set the roofline to a rainbow of the birthday person's favorite colors. Use the "chase" or "wave" animation for a party atmosphere. At midnight, switch to a slow fade to signal the evening winding down. Parents tell us this is one of the most popular features with kids — arriving home to find the house lit up in their colors.

Custom

Valentine's Day Romance

Deep rose pink with soft pink accents and warm white highlights. Use a very slow pulse animation — the lights gently breathe brighter and dimmer, creating a romantic ambiance. Brightness at 40%. This pairs perfectly with a special dinner at home or a surprise arrival.

Pro Tips for Getting the Most from Your Oelo System

1. Use the Scheduling Feature

Don't treat your Oelo lighting like a manual dimmer switch. The app's scheduling feature is the real superpower. Set a "daily driver" theme (warm white or amber) to activate at sunset and turn off at your normal bedtime. Then schedule holiday themes to take over automatically on specific dates. Set it once and forget it — your house will be decorated perfectly for every holiday without you lifting a finger.

2. Layer Zone Colors for Depth

Most homeowners set the entire roofline to one color. But the real magic happens when you use zones. Set the main roofline to a base color, gables and dormers to a contrasting accent color, and the garage to a complementary third color. This creates architectural depth and makes your home look like it was professionally designed (because it was).

3. Adjust Brightness for the Season

Summer evenings are light until 8:30 PM, so your lights need to be brighter to be visible at dusk. Winter sunsets happen as early as 4:30 PM, so lower brightness works fine. Adjust seasonally: summer 40–60%, winter 25–40%, holidays 60–80%.

4. Don't Overuse Animations

Animations are fun for holidays and parties, but they can look busy for daily use. Reserve chase effects, strobes, and rapid color changes for specific occasions. For daily use, static colors or very slow fades are more elegant and won't distract neighbors.

5. Complement with Landscape Lighting

Oelo lights are roofline lights — they highlight the top of your home. For a complete look, pair them with well-placed landscape lighting that illuminates walkways, trees, and garden features. The combination of roofline color and ground-level warm lighting creates a layered, professional outdoor lighting design.

6. Plan Your Schedule in Advance

Sit down in January and map out your entire year of color themes. The Oelo app supports multiple scheduled events, so you can program the whole year in one sitting. When Halloween rolls around in October, your lights will automatically switch to purple and orange — and your neighbors will wonder how you remember to decorate so perfectly every single time.
